scope_statement: Independent, source-grounded reconstruction of software architecture’s structures, interaction/quality reasoning, descriptions, decisions, evaluation, conformance and revision, including documented contemporary translations and criticism. The population is the registered candidate set after examination, not every proposition in every publication.
scope_boundaries: No requester repositories, prior Evolved packets or sibling research consulted.
Architecture intersects but does not annex enterprise, hardware, systems or organisational architecture.
Program families and maintenance are studied only where they establish architecture mechanisms, history or interface obligations; sibling conclusions are not supplied.
This is an explicit bounded interpretive study, not an exhaustive systematic bibliometric review or a meta-analysis.
Normative clauses not read, current vendor prices/quotas not checked, and inaccessible monographs/editions do not support detailed claims.
External legal/compliance authority is not inferred from architectural methods.

saturation_rationale.BASIS: Decision-oriented evidence saturation within the declared scope: all A1–A9 questions and all 68 candidates received sources, criticism, cheap-path/trigger and disposition examination.
EVIDENCE_CHANGED_JUDGEMENTS: Architecture-as-all-important-decisions, mandatory 4+1, standards-as-quality-certificate, review-as-guarantee, deterministic mirroring, zero drift, local-metric self-authorisation and emergence-without-reasoning were not retained as general properties.
The mixed service/REST candidate was superseded and split; recursive driver-based design and a distinct conditional Wright theorem were added after inspection.

Current LLM evidence narrowed assistance and left open-ended autonomy unresolved; current energy evidence retained measurement-bound and constraint-bound sustainability rather than universal green styles.
saturation_rationale.STOPPING_JUDGEMENT: Further equivalent searches were not expected to change the registered mechanism, prerequisite, genealogy distinction or composition guard. New unseen evidence could revise a later revision; this freeze does not claim every publication was retrieved.

genealogy_nodes.PROBLEM_SITUATION: Reason about concurrent system behaviour and make implementation manageable.
genealogy_nodes.MECHANISM: A hierarchy of levels and carefully delimited abstractions organise a small multiprogramming system.
genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: An early concrete account of organising software through abstraction rather than a later architecture-description notation.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: One author-reported system and partial testing; not evidence that all modern layers yield reliability.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: Later architecture discussions share abstraction concerns; direct influence on every branch is not inferred.

genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A semantic criterion for decomposition and an architectural family/change account.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: Change hypotheses can be wrong; the KWIC illustration is not an industrial causal estimate. The 1976 item was inspected as metadata only.

genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A semantic boundary is distinct from a code module or deployment boundary.

genealogy_nodes.SCHOOL_OR_BRANCH: REST as a constrained hypermedia architectural style
genealogy_nodes.PROBLEM_SITUATION: Distributed hypermedia needs evolvability, scalability and interactions among independently developed participants.
genealogy_nodes.MECHANISM: Combine client/server, stateless interaction, cacheability, uniform interface, layering and optional code-on-demand.
genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Uniform-interface constraints include resource identification, representations, self-descriptive messages and hypermedia application state.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: A generic interface sacrifices some application-specific efficiency; REST is not every HTTP service and statelessness does not remove persistent resource state.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: The domain-specific constraint set remains distinguishable from generic service orientation.

genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Awareness, willingness and reachability are not interchangeable with authorisation or successful effect.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: A reference model does not prescribe one stack or establish service economics.

genealogy_nodes.DATE_OR_PERIOD: 2014 account; 2015 caution; 2019 and 2020 field cases; 2024–2026 research
genealogy_nodes.PROBLEM_SITUATION: Large products may need differentiated deployment and team change, but distributed boundaries introduce operational coordination.
genealogy_nodes.MECHANISM: Select deployment boundaries according to genuine independence needs; preserve modularity or consolidate when boundaries supply little benefit.
genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Shopify and Istio show that purposeful internal modules or consolidation can be legitimate outcomes.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: These are context-specific author/project accounts, not randomised comparisons. Benchmark decomposition metrics are not operating outcomes.

genealogy_nodes.SCHOOL_OR_BRANCH: Architectural debt, incremental migration and continuous evaluation
genealogy_nodes.DATE_OR_PERIOD: 1992 debt account; 2014 architecture-debt field study; 2019 guidance; 2024 revised migration essay
genealogy_nodes.PROBLEM_SITUATION: Expedient choices and changing conditions can accumulate costs that a one-off design description conceals.
genealogy_nodes.MECHANISM: Distinguish debt consequences, migrate through viable intermediate states and monitor selected architecture-related conditions.
genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Architecture evaluation and revision can be continuous, and simplification can be an improvement.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: Debt metaphors are not monetary measurements; fitness functions are selected proxies; migration adds coexistence costs.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: The mature form couples observations to revisable decisions rather than preserving every old rule or buying every future option.

genealogy_nodes.PROBLEM_SITUATION: Data, feedback and undeclared consumers cross ordinary software boundaries.
genealogy_nodes.MECHANISM: Treat data/configuration/feedback obligations as architectural dependencies and evaluate system behaviour, not code alone.
genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A documented domain translation of dependency, interface and debt reasoning.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: The 2015 account is practitioner evidence, not a controlled architecture intervention; generated structural proposals do not validate learned-system behaviour.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: Current LLM work expands assistance but does not remove hidden coupling or validation burdens.

genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Serverless is an architectural translation with distinctive constraints, not an automatic simplification or sustainability guarantee.

genealogy_nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Architecture can contribute to sustainability while requiring broader lifecycle/context evidence.
genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: Measured package/DRAM energy is not whole-lifecycle carbon; a rapid review and focus group do not prove universal prescriptions.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: The field supports a bounded concern and exposes evidence gaps rather than establishing one universally green architecture.

genealogy_nodes.LIMITS: Method-author synthesis and guidance are not independent comparative proof; recursion can become premature design expansion.
genealogy_nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_DEVELOPMENT: Small work can use direct alternatives and checks; the fuller method is selected when driver conflicts or scope justify it.

domain_models.TITLE: Architectural significance and concerns
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: A software system, its environment, stakeholder concerns, candidate choices, affected obligations and the evidence believed to support them.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: A choice is significant relative to the reach of its consequences, not a fixed file size or job role. Concerns attach to choices through scenarios/constraints. An authorised decision and an implemented result remain separate state changes.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Users, maintainers, operators and sponsors supply concerns; designers explain consequences; actual authorised participants accept trade-offs; implementers change real artefacts.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Trace a claimed concern through a selected choice to an observation. Agreement shows coordination, not successful operation.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: A short conversation, a few explicit constraints and a check of the real effect can be coherent for one team.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: choosing a colour token is normally local, but a colour-encoding decision becomes architectural when every alarm channel and accessibility commitment depends on it.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Decomposition and interface contracts
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Responsibilities, hidden decisions, model meanings, interfaces, connectors, shared resources and typed dependencies.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: Information hiding partitions knowledge; connector semantics govern interaction; containment constrains propagation. A module boundary, domain context, deployment boundary and team boundary are related but non-identical partitions.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Producers and consumers negotiate meaningful obligations, implement or adapt interfaces, and exercise change/failure cases across them.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: An import graph establishes only its extracted relation. Correctness dependence, shared state and external effects require additional evidence. Wright provides a conditional formal branch, not automatic semantic closure.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: A direct local interface with explicit meaning and a few integration cases; no network boundary is required.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: two services with separate repositories share a global database trigger; their apparent isolation fails when one change alters the other’s invariant.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Quality-attribute trade-offs
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Concern-specific scenarios, response measures, constraints, preferences, mechanisms and environmental assumptions.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: A tactic changes a quality model parameter, not an abstract quality in isolation. The system response depends on interaction with other tactics and workload. Hard limits restrict acceptable options before preference comparison.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Stakeholders define acceptable responses; designers propose interventions; evaluators construct models/tests; operators supply observations.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Use workload, fault and population scope and a declared accounting boundary. The same functional answer can be unacceptable because of latency, information disclosure or resource use.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: One concrete scenario and competing-cost check are sufficient for a narrow reversible decision.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Published: EcoFaaS’s chosen energy/tail-latency benefits coexist with worse mean latency versus its full-frequency baseline; its energy boundary is package/DRAM, not total carbon.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Views and correspondence
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Views of structure, interaction, deployment/development organisation, their viewpoint rules and mappings to realised artefacts.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: A view selects facts for a concern. Correspondences connect elements/relations across views and to implementation; consistency among views is weaker than truth about implementation. Recovery produces hypotheses with provenance.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Different consumers ask different questions. Authors map shared elements and explain differences; analysts inspect source, configuration or traces to check relevant claims.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Formal semantics can establish a model property; relation extraction and implementation refinement have separate obligations. A sampled trace cannot certify every possible runtime path.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: Use the least number of views that answer the concern, with explicit labels and a manual correspondence check.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: a logical service view is consistent with a deployment drawing but both omit a production sidecar that changes network and failure behaviour.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Alternative evaluation
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Feasible alternatives including no change, architectural drivers, scenarios, assumptions, risk/sensitivity findings and costs.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: SAAM emphasises changes; ATAM exposes multi-quality risks; CBAM examines utility/cost under assumptions; prototypes and formal models supply different evidence. They can substitute or complement, not automatically all execute.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Analysis, design synthesis and evaluation interleave: a risk may change requirements, an experiment may reveal a new option, and a local design may proceed while another uncertainty is studied.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Method outputs are not outcomes. Compare alternatives under equivalent conditions and preserve exclusions, weak baselines and uncertainty.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: A focused alternative-and-risk conversation with one discriminating experiment can be enough.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: a successful review is followed by a workload dominated by an omitted write path; the previous non-risk is reopened, not defended by the review’s approval.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Decision knowledge and coordination
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Current decisions, rationale, assumptions, status/history and the people whose work or commitments depend on them.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: Decision dependencies make knowledge transfer useful. Communication requirements follow relevant technical/work coupling, but neither a record nor an organisation chart mechanically produces coherent design.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Teams exchange decisions and exceptions; later actors retrieve rationale; authorised participants revise it when assumptions fail. Reconstructed explanation remains separate from documentary history.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Check a real later question and a real cross-team dependency. Surveys and observational congruence are not universal causal evidence.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: One shared explanation and a short retained note for a non-obvious decision; no board or permanent extra role is inherent.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: a successor can explain why an interface was chosen but discovers a critical workload assumption no longer holds; the old record guides revision rather than preventing it.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Conformance and reconstruction
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Baseline constraints, extracted/observed relations, mappings, deviations, evidence and adjudicated dispositions.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: A conformance result relates one mapping and dependency kind to one baseline. A smell is a candidate risk signal. The target of correction may be code, configuration, description, rule or an unsupported inference.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Analysts report findings; maintainers explain context; authorised reviewers evaluate consequences and change the right artefact. Rechecking establishes whether the actual disposition took effect.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Positive and negative cases expose missed edges and false alarms. Harm requires a current invariant/quality/burden argument, not mere divergence.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: A focused dependency assertion or manual relation comparison with a retained reason for the rule.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: an approved caching improvement violates an old layering rule; if current freshness and security constraints remain satisfied, revise the rule rather than revert for a green count.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

domain_models.TITLE: Architecture evolution and revision
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Current architecture, plausible future variants, transition/coexistence states, debt claims, change evidence and optional runtime controllers.
domain_models.RELATIONAL_ACCOUNT: Change may alter structure, knowledge, baseline or policy. A transition must preserve selected continuity obligations; new evidence can reopen earlier decisions. Runtime adaptation adds a model/action feedback loop whose own assumptions need review.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_COMMUNICATION: Engineers implement and migrate; operators observe actual effects; delegated controllers may execute specified actions. External stakeholders or commitments constrain what those actors may optimise.
domain_models.VALIDITY_AND_OBSERVATION: Tests must cover transition states and post-change consequences. The controller cannot validate itself merely by increasing its score or changing its objective.
domain_models.MINIMAL_CONFIGURATION: Direct reviewed change followed by a relevant observation; richer migration/automation only where continuity or operating variability warrants it.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_EXAMPLE: Analytical: autoscaling reduces latency but exceeds an external resource cap; the transition is not accepted as overall success even though its local metric improved.
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: ANALYTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_GROUNDED_IN_NAMED_SOURCES; not an independently validated unified formalism.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Shared users/invariants require a common meaning across decisions.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Decisions are local, reversible and do not alter others’ obligations.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Share essential contracts and permit independent implementations or explicit translations.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A supposedly local exception changes a shared invariant, or shared rules expand to stylistic micromanagement.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can this choice change an external consumer’s required behaviour or meaning? If yes, negotiate that consequence; otherwise leave it local.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Which semantics truly need common ownership is often contested.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Indirection and runtime overhead versus propagated change and exposed implementation knowledge.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: A credible recurring change can be insulated by a stable semantic contract.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: The direct mechanism is stable, cheap to change and clearer for its consumers.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Expose relevant behaviour/diagnostics while hiding the varying implementation choice.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: An interface hides information the consumer needs for correctness or diagnosis, or abstraction predicts the wrong changes.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Try the likely change and a realistic diagnosis/performance case; compare affected obligations and overhead.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Future change frequency and debugging cost cannot always be predicted.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Paid flexibility premium versus potentially expensive later migration.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Repeated credible variants or changes have high rework costs.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Future variants are speculative and later correction remains cheap.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Implement stable seams for plausible changes while deferring unused generality.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Seams leak semantics or temporary flexibility becomes a permanent platform without consumers.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: What evidence makes this change likely, and which break-even assumptions would reverse the investment?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Neither blanket anticipation nor blanket deferral dominates every domain.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Slow review, stale models and opportunity cost versus undetected consequential errors.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Failure consequences are high, model assumptions tractable and stronger evidence can change the decision.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: A small reversible choice is already understood and extra analysis adds little information.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Analyse the risky interaction formally and evaluate the remaining design with focused scenarios/prototypes.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: The formal island ignores the actual failure boundary or a rushed lightweight review omits a critical scenario.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Will the added method discriminate feasible options or protect an otherwise unexamined severe consequence?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: There is no validated universal effort threshold.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Unreviewed erosion versus entrenching obsolete constraints.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: The baseline still protects a current invariant or external commitment.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: The baseline’s rationale no longer holds and an alternative preserves or improves current obligations.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Adjudicate deviations and revise implementation or baseline with explicit rationale.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Convenient exception names hide harm, or perfect conformance is rewarded despite worsening outcomes.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which currently valid concern would this deviation harm, and what evidence supports that link?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown long-term consequences may keep the deviation unresolved.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Coordination/transaction cost versus inconsistent state or meaning.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: A shared invariant genuinely requires coordinated action across participants.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Local changes can be decoupled without violating the consumer’s obligations.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Use the weakest coordination sufficient for the actual invariant, with explicit compensations only when acceptable.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Compensation cannot undo an external effect; eventual consistency is used for a constraint that requires immediate validity.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can a temporarily inconsistent or irreversible state be accepted by the actual affected consumer?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Invariant ownership and acceptable inconsistency require contextual authority.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Cheap signal and scale versus false positives, self-reported metrics and missing paths.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: The indicator is calibrated and can prioritise a large repeated problem.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: The target is small or the proxy is too disconnected from the consequence.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Automate candidate detection and independently adjudicate high-consequence conclusions.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Human review rubber-stamps a score, or verification cost exceeds saved effort.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Does the signal predict the actual concern on positive, negative and changed-condition cases, and at what total cost?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Ground-truth datasets and natural operational base rates can be missing.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Adaptation overhead and controller risk versus lost opportunity under changing demand.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Conditions vary and bounded actions preserve explicitly checked constraints.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Observations/actions are unreliable or the safe static arrangement is adequate.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Constrain objectives, monitor post-change effects and permit reviewed policy updates.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A local gain breaks an external limit or the controller edits away its own evidence requirement.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Is the realised transition inside a currently justified acceptance envelope, not merely better on its objective?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Multiple interacting controllers and changing objectives remain difficult.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Turnover/reconstruction burden versus obsolete or unread records.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Non-obvious decisions must survive handovers or distributed coordination.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: One stable team shares sufficient context for local reversible decisions.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Short linked records for consequential decisions with clear status and retirement criteria.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Many short records become an unindexed archive or reconstructed stories masquerade as contemporary history.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can a plausible later consumer answer the consequential question without rediscovery, and what does upkeep cost?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Causal return on record keeping varies and is poorly estimated.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Translation/variation-management cost versus repeated independent implementation.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Related contexts share stable obligations and the reuse mechanism preserves them.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Semantics or operating qualities differ enough that adaptation defeats the saving.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Share compatible mechanisms while keeping distinct semantic models and explicit adapters.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A universal framework silently assumes a common control model or feature combination that does not exist.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which exact assumptions are shared, and what must be translated or ruled out for the intended composition?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Cross-family benefits require product/maintenance evidence beyond this lane.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: One-team stable application versus long-lived multi-team product
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: Two systems have comparable functionality; one has stable shared understanding and cheap local change, the other many teams, turnover and cross-boundary commitments.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: The small team uses ordinary code review plus a few consequential checks. The multi-team product preserves interface obligations, decisions and correspondence where consumers need them.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: Whether consequential decisions are actually understood and whether changes violate another consumer’s commitments.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: No mandatory architecture office, multi-view package or ADR per edit. More coordination is warranted only where the second context creates a real dependency.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: The supposedly simple application acquires a critical external contract, or the multi-team artefacts have no demonstrable consumer.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Identical functional output, different operating qualities
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: Two implementations return the same answers, but one times out under the required load and another consumes an unacceptable resource budget.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Evaluate the declared response measures under the relevant load and resource boundary; choose a feasible trade-off rather than output equivalence alone.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: Latency distribution, throughput/failure behaviour and the actual resource measure under stated conditions.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: Functional equivalence is insufficient for the architecture choice. The relevant quality constraints can discriminate.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: The load or resource boundary is unrepresentative, or neither implementation can satisfy the external constraint.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Authorised improvement violates an obsolete rule
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: An old layering rule forbids a new dependency; a reviewed replacement preserves the protected invariant with lower cost.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Investigate the finding, confirm authority and real effect, then supersede the rule/mapping rather than force the old structure.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: The invariant still holds; obsolete consumers are absent; the new relation is represented accurately.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: Deviation is not automatically erosion. Conformance supplies a finding, not a veto over justified evolution.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: The old rule protected an overlooked security or failure boundary, or the proposed change was not actually authorised.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Apparently isolated component with hidden shared state
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: Two separately deployed services share a mutable table and are forced to release together whenever its interpretation changes.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Inspect semantic/data dependencies. Either enforce the needed independence or accept a coordinated unit rather than count deployments as isolation.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: A representative schema/semantic change and fault demonstrate the actual propagation boundary.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: Naming and process separation do not establish operational independence. A modular monolith or explicit shared contract may dominate.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: A genuine independent scaling/failure constraint makes consolidation unacceptable; stronger data contracts may instead be justified.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Successful review, unrepresentative workload
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: An architecture review finds no major risks for a small steady workload; production has bursty traffic and a previously omitted failure mode.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Treat the new evidence as a reason to reopen scenarios and the affected choice, not as proof the review procedure was faithfully predictive.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: Production-relevant load/fault observations, with the earlier assumptions retained for comparison.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: The review’s coordination/risk-discovery result can remain real while its operational prediction is invalid outside scope.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: The supposed production observation is itself sampled or misattributed; causal contribution requires separating changed architecture from unrelated interventions.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Runtime adaptation improves a metric and violates an external constraint
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: A controller saves energy by consolidating work but exceeds a non-negotiable response-time or separation constraint.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Exclude the action from admissible policies, restore an acceptable state and examine the policy/model observation boundary.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: Both energy and the external constraint after the actual change, not the controller’s own score.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: Local improvement neither authorises the change nor establishes whole-system improvement.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: The external constraint was actually negotiable under the authorised trade-off and the new response is within that agreed range.

analytical_case_tests.TITLE: Failed observation creates a fictitious successful adaptation
analytical_case_tests.SITUATION: A stale probe reports a healthy node after the actuator has failed to move work.
analytical_case_tests.SELECTED_ACTION_OR_NON_ACTION: Suspend the unsupported claim, use independent state evidence or a safe fallback, and repair the observation/actuation mapping.
analytical_case_tests.REQUIRED_OBSERVATION: Real deployment and request behaviour establish whether the action happened and whether constraints hold.
analytical_case_tests.COMPOSED_SYSTEM_VERDICT: A model transition is not a real transition. The composed account fails closed on the claim, not by pretending all operation can stop without cost.
analytical_case_tests.WHAT_WOULD_DEFEAT_THE_VERDICT: A bounded degraded mode is unavailable; the residual operating risk then requires explicit accountable judgement rather than fictional assurance.
